summary: Brick tower on a 1895 caisson in Kedges Straits, Chesapeake Bay; the 1875 screw-pile light was wrecked by ice in 1893, and the keepers' house is gone.

light.characteristic: flashing white with two red sectors

structures.note: Square cottage-style screw-pile; bent over by ice in January 1893 (cheslights), wreck recorded as lost 1893 (LHB).
Cast-iron foundation cylinder 25 ft across on a steel caisson (LHB FY1896); tower 47 ft above the water (USLHS).
Demolished soon after automation because of fire and vandalism danger (cheslights); date not given.

access.note: Not open to the public (USLHS). Reached only by boat or plane (cheslights).

events.note: Square cottage-style screw-pile light built on the shoal, replacing the Fog Point light (built 1827)
Ice wrecks the screw-pile light in January (LHB narrative) or by 2 February (LHB bell list); the house is not carried from its site but is knocked over
Appropriation of $30,000 by act of 3 March 1893 to reestablish the light
Temporary lens-lantern light placed on the wreck in June 1893 to mark it at night
Act of 21 December 1893 allows a caisson structure, paid from the Wolf Trap balance
Caisson light: brick tower on a cast-iron cylinder and steel caisson; caisson positioned 20 May 1895
Remains of the old wreck and its temporary lamp carried away by ice in winter 1894-95
Fourth-order lens from Cherrystone Bar Light installed; the fifth-order lens goes to Cherrystone
Converted to automatic operation; Coast Guard keepers reassigned

corrections.proposed: tower, caisson, brick, built 1895, 14.3 m (47 ft above water), standing
corrections.why: 1875 was the screw-pile light, wrecked by ice in 1893. The present brick caisson tower was built in 1895 (LHB FY1896; USLHS place record; cheslights).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The 1875 light was a screw-pile and the present light a 1895 caisson on the same spot. The record's first year and the current tower's year are both right for different structures.
The record's Fl W 6s is a short form. Cheslights gives the current light as a flashing white with two red sectors, which the record's short form leaves out.

The Board's FY1893 narrative says January 1893; its fog-signal list gives 2 February 1893; the Annapolis paper of 6 February reported that word reached the Board the day before. The sources disagree on the month; the list and the paper point to early February.

notes_for_editor: Length is moderate: four Light-House Board reports, two Annapolis/Baltimore newspapers, the Chesapeake Chapter heritage page and the USLHS record. (1) Owner and maintaining agency are not named in any source I could read; the record has none. (2) The NRHP number in the record (02001422) is not verified: the NPGallery PDF returned a placeholder image, and a search snippet of the USCG Historian's page (not read; the page returns 403 through the archive) says the station was judged not eligible for the Register because the keepers' quarters were demolished. Check before printing any NRHP claim. (3) Wreck month: the 1893 narrative says January, the bell list says 2 February. (4) The 1896 volume repeats the lens-lantern discontinuance with the date 22 February 1896 (scan p. 89 and p. 147); the story says so; a human should decide whether that is a second loss or a repeated entry. (5) Keeper names are the USLHS roster's transcription (the archive's own warning: confirm each keeper in a primary record); none was confirmed separately. The 1893 keeper who abandoned the station is not named in the newspaper. (6) 1916 'Henry E. Sterling' versus the roster's 'Henry C. Sterling': not confirmed to be the same man. The merit-medal list's reason is not visible in the OCR I read. (7) Cheslights gives the lens in 1919 as fourth-order; the USLHS record gives the current optic as 200 mm without an order. (8) Fog Point is placed on Cherry Island by cheslights; Wikipedia places the earlier light on Smith Island. Only the 1827 date and 'about a mile to the south' are used. (9) Wikipedia was used only for leads (five-legged screw-pile, octagonal house, 1919/1950 dates) and none of its claims is cited. (10) The 1875 newspaper's 43 ft and Tros' Marshes are as printed; the site in Virginia is not identified. (11) Quotation of German: the English rendering of the 1875 and 1916 passages is mine. Fact-check 2026-10-22: the 1893 word read 'overturned' is OCR-garbled in the Board's text ('[>uHlied over'); the 1896 'February 22, 1896' list entry is an OCR reading (two copies agree); the scan page 103 for the 1896 report is not confirmed by the corpus index; page images were not viewed.
